lens: responsive mobile task completion, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The final local build completed responsive checks at 375x812, 390x844, 430x932, and 844x390 with no horizontal overflow, no visible target below 44 pixels, and zero console errors. Verified action, unknown recovery, conflict/history, deletion recovery, 200-percent text, dark mode, reduced motion, focus order, and mobile Escape are directly covered. A real virtual keyboard, VoiceOver, background/relaunch, and physical-device browser behavior remain untested.
findings.user_impact: Responsive Web is highly usable in emulation, but assistive and device-lifecycle reliability is not yet proven for a paid promise.
findings.recommendation: Run the full production loop on a small and large physical phone with VoiceOver, accessibility text, virtual keyboard, landscape, background, relaunch, and an interrupted retry.
findings.verification: Evidence, identity, review, approval, unknown recovery, history, and deletion remain named, ordered, reachable, unclipped, and duplicate-free across the physical-device matrix.

strengths: The first task, relationship state, and one next action remain legible at 375 and 390 pixels.
The fixed navigation and boundary-case footer no longer intercept the final sidebar action.
Conflict history and verified outcome remain readable in landscape without horizontal scrolling.
Every visible interactive target in the final viewport matrix meets the 44-pixel floor.
missing_evidence: Real virtual-keyboard and physical-device background/relaunch evidence.
A complete authenticated production mobile loop.
open_questions: Does the bottom dock remain non-obstructive when a real keyboard and accessibility text are active together?
